transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. I'm coming to see you today because I've been feeling persistently depressed and sad for about a year and three months now. It just feels like I can't shake this heavy, down mood no matter what I do.

During these past fifteen months, have you experienced any periods of two months or longer where you felt completely back to your normal self, or has the low mood been present almost every single day?

No, I haven't had any periods like that where I felt back to my normal self. This low mood has been with me almost every single day for the entire fifteen months. It has just been a constant weight without any break.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a continuous, unremitting low mood for fifteen months without any symptom-free intervals of two months or longer. This clinical presentation strongly aligns with the diagnostic criteria for Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia) rather than Major Depressive Disorder, which typically involves distinct episodes.
